name: banking
best_for: Education first, deal values in every bullet, and Skills & Interests at the bottom. The one page bulge brackets and boutiques expect.
interview_style: Talk like a sharp, warm friend who's genuinely into their story, never a corporate form. VOICE: keep replies to 1-3 short sentences and ask ONE thing at a time; acknowledge what they just shared by NAMING it specifically ('a SPAN risk model at CME, that's strong'), not with empty filler; use their first name once you know it. When you ask for something, add a half-line on WHY it helps. BANNED openers that read as a robot/script: 'Perfect , ', 'Got it', 'Great!', 'Awesome', 'absolutely', 'no worries', 'for sure', 'to be honest', 'as I mentioned', a bare 'I understand', vary your phrasing, never reuse an opener two turns running. Go BROAD first (invite a story), then narrow to the specifics the CV needs. For accomplishments, gently draw out Situation-Task-Action-Result so bullets end up concrete and, where they exist, quantified. Never interrogate or re-ask something already answered. Invent nothing, use only what they actually tell you. PUNCTUATION: never use an em dash or an en dash. Not one, anywhere. They read as machine-written and the person has asked for them gone three times. Use a comma, a full stop, or a new sentence instead. DOMAIN: this is a banking CV, so draw out the SIZE of things. A deal without a dollar value is invisible to a banking reader, so when they mention a transaction, financing, or portfolio, ask what it was worth and what they personally did on it.

interests.label: Interests
interests.goal: Genuine interests for the bottom line of a banking resume. Interviewers open with these, so they need to be real and specific.
leads: What could you happily lose a Saturday to? Interviewers almost always open with this line, so it is worth getting right.
Any sports, teams, or things you have kept up for years?
What would someone find out about you over a coffee that is not on the resume?

roles.title: Investment Banking Analyst, Mergers and Acquisitions
bullets: Executed four sell-side and two buy-side transactions with a combined value of $2.1 billion across industrials and business services.

Built the operating, DCF and LBO models for the $450 million sale of a specialty chemicals company to a strategic buyer, including synergy cases that supported a final price 12 percent above the first-round bids.
Drafted confidential information memoranda, management presentations and board materials for senior bankers and clients.
Managed virtual data rooms and coordinated diligence across 40 buyers, legal counsel and accountants, answering more than 600 diligence requests on a six-week timeline.
Ran comparable-company and precedent-transaction analyses used in 15 pitch books.
Mentored two incoming analysts on modeling standards and pitch-book production.

roles.title: Investment Banking Summer Analyst
bullets: Supported a $600 million debt refinancing for a healthcare services client, building the credit statistics, covenant headroom and downside sensitivity analysis used in the lender presentation.
Prepared industry overviews and trading comparables for three pitches in consumer and retail.
Screened 120 potential acquirers for a sell-side mandate and wrote buyer profiles for the top 30.
Built a sum-of-the-parts valuation for a diversified manufacturer weighing the spin-off of its aerospace segment.
Updated the group's weekly deal tracker and market update for the managing directors.
Received a full-time return offer at the end of the program.

roles.title: Equity Research Intern
bullets: Built and maintained earnings models for six mid-cap industrial companies and drafted quarterly earnings notes, publishing each note within a day of the company report.
Wrote an initiation-of-coverage section on a logistics company that the senior analyst published.
Tracked channel checks and industry data in a weekly sector dashboard used by the research team.
Joined management calls and summarized guidance changes for the morning meeting within an hour of each release.

roles.title: Portfolio Analyst
bullets: Pitched three long positions to the investment committee with full valuation and risk cases, two of them added to a $1.5 million student-managed portfolio that beat its benchmark by 3 points.
Led the consumer sector team of five analysts through weekly coverage reviews.
Rebuilt the fund's performance-attribution workbook used in the annual report to trustees.

roles.title: Finance Intern
bullets: Built a loan-pricing model for small-business lending that weighed risk grade, collateral and term, adopted by the credit committee for the following year.
Reconciled monthly loan portfolio reports and flagged $250,000 in misclassified balances for correction.
Prepared the deposit-growth section of the quarterly board package.
